channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Advogado inclui Zuckerberg, Bill Gates e Vini Jr. em ação dos “clones”
item.description: Lawyer Kelmo Martins Bandeira has asked the STF to include Mark Zuckerberg, Bill Gates, and Vini Jr. in a lawsuit alleging an international DNA cloning scheme, which already involves Lula, Bolsonaro, Pope Leo XIV, and Leonardo DiCaprio. He also demands monthly indemnities and a share of revenues from companies like Meta, Microsoft, and Ambev, despite presenting no scientific evidence or proof. The newly added individuals were labeled 'Judas Escariotes' by the lawyer.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da nota do governo Lula contra o tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government condemned the 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian products as a "regrettable milestone" in bilateral relations, stating there is no justification for the unilateral measure and announcing it will pursue WTO dispute mechanisms and apply the Reciprocity Law. The Planalto noted the U.S. has accumulated a $424.5 billion surplus with Brazil over the past 15 years and defended policies like Pix and reduced deforestation since 2023.

item.title: Governo Lula chama tarifaço dos EUA de “marco lastimável”
item.description: The Brazilian government labeled the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods a "regrettable milestone" in bilateral relations and said it will invoke the Reciprocity Law and bring the case to the WTO. It rejected U.S. claims of unfair practices, citing low effective tariffs and a historical U.S. trade surplus with Brazil, while accusing the Bolsonaro family of advancing electoral interests against Brazil's national interest.

item.title: 'Lula colocou seu ego à frente', diz Marco Rubio sobre novas tarifas
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed President Lula for putting his ego ahead of national interests following the announcement of a new 25% tariff on Brazilian goods by the USTR. Rubio claimed the measure resulted from Brazil's alleged intransigence in trade negotiations.

item.title: Governo Lula diz que vai acionar Lei de Reciprocidade contra tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government announced it will immediately invoke the Reciprocity Law in response to new U.S. import tariffs on Brazilian goods. Approved unanimously by Congress, the measure aims to ensure trade reciprocity and protect national interests against what Brazil views as a unilateral and harmful action by the United States.

item.title: Tarifaço é enredo construído pela família Bolsonaro, diz governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government accused the Bolsonaro family of actively collaborating with the U.S. investigation that led to a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, calling it part of a politically motivated 'plot' driven by electoral interests. The Presidency's Secretariat of Social Communication stated that defending national sovereignty transcends ideology and that the government will not hesitate to protect the country's interests.

item.title: Tarifaço: Rubio diz que Lula põe seu ego na frente
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized President Lula, claiming the Brazilian government failed to negotiate in good faith with the United States and that Lula's economic policies are harmful to both Americans and Brazilians. Rubio stated that Lula prioritized his own ego over reaching a beneficial agreement for the Brazilian people, and that the proposed 25% USTR tariffs on Brazilian goods are the price of that stance.

item.title: Leia a íntegra do documento do tarifaço de 25% a produtos do Brasil
item.description: The U.S. imposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods effective July 22, 2026, following a Section 301 investigation that cited unfair trade practices, including alleged advantages of Brazil’s Pix system over U.S. payment firms. The move was anticipated by the Lula administration, which is now considering retaliatory measures. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro attended the public hearing as an observer, but his testimony did not alter the outcome.

item.title: Lula colocou ego à frente do povo brasileiro, diz Rubio sobre tarifas
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the new 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods are a retaliation for what he described as the Lula administration’s lack of good-faith negotiations, claiming the president prioritized his ego over the well-being of the Brazilian people. The tariffs, which took effect after a Section 301 investigation, target sectors like digital payments and exclude beef and coffee. Brazil is considering reciprocal measures as bilateral trade tensions escalate.

item.title: Tarifaço: Brasil aciona Lei da Reciprocidade e levará EUA à OMC
item.description: Brazil announced it will immediately invoke the Reciprocity Law against the U.S. and revive the case at the WTO following Washington's imposition of a 25% additional tariff on Brazilian goods under Section 301. The government labeled the U.S. measure illegal and arbitrary, citing a cumulative U.S. trade surplus of $424.5 billion with Brazil over the last 15 years and noting that 76% of American products entered Brazil duty-free in 2025. The response combines external commercial pressure with an internal political offensive, blaming the 'active collaboration of the Bolsonaro family' for the failure of negotiations.

item.title: Rubio diz Brasil foi tarifado em 25% porque Lula não negociou com os EUA de boa-fé
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for the U.S. decision to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, claiming Brazil was targeted due to a lack of good faith in trade negotiations. The tariff was announced by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR).

item.title: Reciprocidade e crítica aos Bolsonaro: A reação do governo Lula após EUA anunciar tarifaço de 25%
item.description: The Lula government condemned the U.S. decision to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, arguing there is no justification given the U.S. trade surplus with Brazil and announcing it will invoke the Reciprocity Law to impose countermeasures. The government also accused Bolsonaro allies of supporting the tariffs for electoral motives, labeling them 'false patriots'.

item.title: Lula não negociou de boa fé com os EUA e colocou ego acima de acordo, diz Rubio
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused President Lula of failing to negotiate in good faith with the United States and prioritizing his ego over a trade agreement, following the imposition of 25% tariffs on Brazilian imports. The Lula government condemned the move, stating it will invoke the Reciprocity Law and criticized the Bolsonaro family, while industry groups warn the tariffs threaten Brazilian export competitiveness.

item.title: 'Marco lastimável': Planalto acionará reciprocidade ante tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government described Donald Trump's announcement of a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods on July 15, 2026, as a 'sad milestone' in Brazil-U.S. relations. The Planalto stated it will invoke reciprocity in response to the U.S. trade measure.

item.title: Brasil vai acionar reciprocidade contra taxa dos EUA: "Marco lastimável"
item.description: The Lula government announced Brazil will activate the Reciprocity Law in response to the U.S. imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, calling the move a 'lamentable milestone' in bilateral relations. The government rejects the legitimacy of the USTR investigation, cites data showing the U.S. has maintained a $424.5 billion trade surplus with Brazil over 15 years, and notes that most private-sector interventions in public hearings opposed the tariff. The statement also attributes the U.S. decision to the influence of the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Governo Lula reage ao tarifaço, promete reciprocidade e culpa família Bolsonaro
item.description: The Lula government labeled the U.S. decision to raise tariffs on Brazilian products as "regrettable," threatening reciprocal measures and blaming the Bolsonaro family for escalating trade tensions. The official statement said July 15, 2026, will be remembered as a negative milestone in Brazil-U.S. relations.

item.title: Tarifaço tira de Flávio o trunfo de Trump e deixa fatura para Lula
item.description: Donald Trump's new tariff hike harmed both Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula: the former lost his key electoral argument of proximity to Washington as a political asset, while the latter bore the political responsibility for Brazil's diplomatic failure to prevent the measure. Despite five high-level meetings involving Itamaraty, MDIC, and presidential advisors, the tariff was maintained, leaving the productive sector in a seven-day negotiation window without guaranteed solutions. Flávio learned that access to Trump does not equate to influence, while Lula risks facing the political cost if the tariff impacts jobs and orders.

item.title: Rubio diz que Lula não negociou com os EUA de "boa-fé" sobre tarifas
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed that President Lula's government did not negotiate in good faith regarding tariffs, following the imposition of a 25% duty on most Brazilian imports. He blamed Lula for putting his ego ahead of the Brazilian people's welfare, stating the tariffs are the price of that failure. The tariff takes effect on July 22, with exemptions for coffee, organic honey, and açaí, while ethanol, farm machinery, and clothing remain subject to the duty.

item.title: Após EUA anunciarem novas taxas ao Brasil, governo diz que decisão é 'marco lastimável' nas relações entre os dois países
item.description: The Brazilian government labeled the U.S. decision to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods as a 'regrettable milestone' in bilateral relations, calling it unjustified and inconsistent with multilateral trade rules. Brazil announced it will invoke its Reciprocity Law at the WTO and defended Pix, environmental policies, and digital regulation against U.S. allegations. Certain products, including beef, chicken, coffee, and orange, will be exempt from the tariffs.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest: Lula, Flávio e a direita na pausa para a hidratação - O Assunto #1762
item.description: The Quaest poll released on August 15 shows Lula (PT) leading with 40% in the first round and 45% in the second round against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who has 28% and 37% respectively. Lula is regaining support among independent and young voters, while Flávio is losing ground among non-bolsonarist right-wing voters, suggesting this group may seek alternatives. The survey also found that 42% agree more with Michelle Bolsonaro after videos in which she claimed to have been humiliated by the senator, compared to 18% who support Flávio.

item.title: Planalto prevê que governo Trump vai 'pausar' negociações com o Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian government anticipates that the Trump administration will pause trade negotiations with Brazil following new U.S. tariff increases, viewing the move as the culmination of a political tension that began a year ago. This protectionist stance is seen as an escalation in bilateral relations, with potential consequences for Brazilian exports.

item.title: Visita ao Poder360: Nelsinho Trad
item.description: Senator Nelsinho Trad (PSD-MS) visited the Poder360 headquarters in Brasília on Wednesday (Jul 15, 2026) and gave a live interview. He discussed U.S. tariff increases, the proposal to classify criminal factions as terrorists, and confirmed his pre-candidacy for re-election.

item.title: Tarifaço de Trump virou cabo de guerra entre Lula e Flávio antes das eleições
item.description: The threat of U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods has become a political battleground between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of the 2026 elections. While Lula’s government prefers to delay negotiations until after the vote, Flávio traveled to the U.S. to oppose the tariffs, arguing that imposing them now would unfairly punish those who supported the measures. His team claims he advocated for postponing the decision until after October to protect Brazilian exporters.

item.title: Petistas defendem Lula após Flávio citar foto com Deolane
item.description: Lula’s supporters defended him after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) used a photo of Lula with influencer Deolane Bezerra—arrested on money laundering suspicions for the PCC—to counter criticism of his own photo with Luiz Philipi Mourão (‘Sicário’), alleged by the PF to lead a militia for Banco Master founder Daniel Vorcaro. Flávio implied Lula associates with criminals, while his team said he routinely takes photos with the public. X users widely criticized the comparison as misleading and unfair.

item.title: Governo Lula e Trump tiveram mais de 30 reuniões antes de tarifaço
item.description: The Brazilian government held over 30 meetings with U.S. authorities since July 2025, following Trump’s threat to impose a 50% tariff on Brazilian goods. Despite diplomatic efforts led by Elias and Vieira, the U.S. confirmed a 25% tariff and rejected negotiations, leaving Brazilian officials with the sense that the tariff will remain. The last meeting was with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, with no significant progress.

item.title: Governo Lula avalia que tarifaço de Trump só será negociado após as eleições
item.description: The Lula government believes the U.S. will delay negotiating the 25% tariff on Brazilian goods until after the October elections, betting on a Flávio Bolsonaro victory to secure more favorable concessions. The administration views Bolsonaro as more aligned with Trump’s commercial interests, while Lula would maintain the current trade policy grounded in multilateralism and WTO rules, refusing to compromise on measures like Pix or the taxation of American ethanol.

item.title: Reuniões com autoridades e audiências: relembre tentativas frustradas do governo Lula de evitar novo tarifaço
item.description: The Lula administration attempted, through meetings with U.S. officials and public hearings, to prevent the implementation of a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods by the United States, but negotiations failed. Despite initial praise from Trump after a May meeting and efforts by ministers such as Márcio Elias Rosa and Dario Durigan, the Brazilian government could not reverse the decision, which will significantly impact exports. The possibility of reciprocity has not been detailed, as the list of affected products remains uncertain.

item.title: Retaliação, negociações e exceções: como o Brasil pode reagir a novo tarifaço de Trump
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a response strategy to the new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products, evaluating retaliation, political negotiations with Trump, and inclusion of strategic goods in an exception list that already exempts 73 items such as coffee and meat. The administration is also considering invoking the Economic Reciprocity Law to impose countermeasures, including tariffs on U.S. imports and intellectual property restrictions—a sector highly sensitive to the U.S.

item.title: Equipe econômica avalia que pacote de socorro a tarifaço dos EUA deve ser pontual
item.description: Lula's economic team is evaluating whether a new relief package for Brazilian exporters affected by U.S. tariffs will be needed, and if so, it would be modest and targeted — unlike the larger 'Brazil Sovereign' plan of 2025. The macroeconomic impact of the new U.S. tariffs is expected to remain limited, as Brazil has adapted through market diversification and prior support measures. The Secretariat of Economic Policy has already factored the tariffs into its projections, citing minimal direct effect on GDP due to the U.S. accounting for less than 2% of Brazil's pre-shock exports.

item.title: Estados Unidos anunciam tarifa de 25% sobre produtos brasileiros, mas com exceções
item.description: The U.S. announced a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, with exemptions for beef, orange juice, coffee, petroleum, gas, and aerospace components, among others. The measure takes effect on July 22 and follows a Section 301 investigation by the USTR into alleged unfair trade practices by Brazil. The Lula government says the tariff will only be negotiated after the 2026 elections.

item.title: Moraes assume STF interinamente e mantém sombra sobre bolsonarismo às vésperas da eleição
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes assumes the interim presidency of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) during the judiciary's recess, maintaining his influence over Bolsonarism ahead of the 2026 elections. Four years after presiding over the TSE in the 2022 presidential race, he remains the Bolsonarists' main adversary in the Supreme Court.

item.title: Senado aprova inclusão de educação financeira nos currículos dos ensinos fundamental e médio
item.description: The Federal Senate approved a bill to include financial education as a cross-cutting subject in elementary and high school curricula, covering conscious consumption, pensions, taxes, and insurance. The proposal, authored by federal deputy Any Ortiz (Cidadania-RS), was amended by Senator Teresa Leitão (PT-PE) and returns to the Chamber of Deputies for revalidation before presidential sanction. The goal is to prepare students to make conscious economic decisions and avoid future indebtedness.

item.title: Queda de Flávio na direita não bolsonarista causa apreensão, mas campanha não abre de ofensiva contra o STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) campaign is facing declining support among non-bolsonarist right-wing and independent voters, per a Genial/Quaest poll showing support dropped from 74% to 54% since May. Despite this setback, the campaign maintains its strategy of confronting the STF, particularly Minister Alexandre de Moraes, to energize the bolsonarist base, while also pursuing institutional dialogue — such as a May meeting with STF President Edson Fachin — and proposing policies targeting women and debt relief to attract centro-direita voters.

item.title: Governo Lula se preparou para cenário hostil após EUA anunciar novo tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government prepared for a hostile trade scenario with the U.S. following the announcement of new tariffs against Brazil, defining certain economic points as non-negotiable to safeguard national sovereignty and economic stability.

item.title: Flávio cita Lula com Deolane para rebater selfie com Sicário
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro cited Lula’s relationship with Deolane Bezerra to defend his own photo with Luiz Philipi Mourão, known as 'Sicário', arguing that public figures receive daily photo requests and that the image does not prove illicit ties. He implied Lula maintains connections with criminal-linked individuals, referencing Deolane’s arrest for alleged money laundering for the PCC. Mourão, an employee of Banco Master’s founder Daniel Vorcaro, was identified by the PF as part of an 'intimidation nucleus' targeting opponents, receiving R$1 million monthly for illicit services.

item.title: Fiesp critica governo e diz que tarifaço poderia ter sido evitado
item.description: Fiesp criticized the Lula government's diplomatic conduct, stating that the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods could have been avoided with a more technical and pragmatic approach. The federation argued the measure harms Brazil's competitiveness by unilaterally targeting the country, particularly affecting high-value-added products that rely heavily on the U.S. market.

item.title: Senado fará duas semanas de esforço concentrado após recesso
item.description: The Senate will hold two weeks of concentrated effort after the parliamentary recess (August 10-14 and August 31-September 3) to vote on priority proposals, aligned with the Chamber. The 6x1 PEC, which would reduce the workweek, was postponed until after the recess and is unlikely to take effect before the October elections, despite its electoral appeal for Lula’s government. Other proposals, including Central Bank autonomy, MEI revenue cap increase, and misogyny criminalization, will also be delayed until the second semester.

item.title: Presidente do PT sai em defesa de Jaques Wagner: "Ele tem história e dignidade"
item.description: The national president of the PT, Edinho Silva, defended Senator Jaques Wagner during an event in Salvador, highlighting his trajectory of dignity and honesty amid investigations linked to Banco Master. He stated Wagner is a source of pride for the party and that time and Bahia’s voters will determine the truth, despite a poll showing 37% of Brazilians view the case as having a very negative impact on Lula’s campaign.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro aciona TSE contra pesquisa da AtlasIntel
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign team filed a complaint with the TSE to challenge an AtlasIntel poll released on June 25 showing Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead in the 2026 presidential race, citing the institute’s failure to submit legally required documentation, including municipal breakdowns, sector-specific respondent numbers, and demographic sample composition, rendering the results unauditable. This marks the second such challenge by Bolsonaro’s team against AtlasIntel in 2026, following a successful suspension in May of another poll tied to audio leaks involving the senator and businessman Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio usará veto a visita para reforçar papel de porta-voz de Bolsonaro e isolar Michelle
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign plans to use the veto on contact between him and his father, Jair Bolsonaro, to strengthen his image as the ex-president's main spokesperson and politically isolate Michelle Bolsonaro. The strategy aims to consolidate Flávio's leadership within the PL, diminishing Michelle's influence in the bolsonarist movement. Campaign operatives say the intentional distancing avoids leadership conflicts and centralizes the narrative around Flávio as the natural successor.

item.title: “Jamais desagradaria meu pai”, diz Flávio sobre atrito com Michelle
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro said the public rift with Michelle Bolsonaro could have been avoided if she weren’t the wife of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and stressed his respect for both, stating he would never do anything to displease his father. He also said he avoided watching Michelle’s video in which she claimed to feel humiliated, to prevent being influenced by its content, and downplayed the conflict in light of Brazil’s economic challenges.

item.title: Por que aliados de Lula veem subida do petista nas pesquisas com cautela
item.description: Lula's allies view his polling improvements cautiously, despite him leading with 40% in the first round and 45% in the second against Flávio Bolsonaro's 28% and 37%. Government approval rose to 48%, slightly above disapproval at 47%, but officials consider the gain insufficient given the R$200 billion in economic stimulus. Analyst Robson Bonin notes that while policies like Desenrola are well-received (over 60% approval), the effort invested outweighs the modest gains in voter perception.

item.title: Saiba quais itens vão ficar de fora do tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: President Donald Trump signed a decree on July 15, 2026, imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, while exempting meat and coffee from the measures. The tariffs followed the conclusion of a Section 301 investigation into Brazil’s trade practices, including allegations of unfair advantages for Pix and restrictions on ethanol market access. The Lula government called the tariffs unfair and removed Pix from negotiations, despite not sending officials to prior public hearings.

item.title: Governo Lula encara novo tarifaço dos EUA, mais difícil de derrubar
item.description: The Lula government faces a new U.S. tariff hike, imposing a 25% surtax on Brazilian goods under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, which is seen as harder to reverse due to its strong legal foundation and political backing from Brazil’s opposition linked to the White House ahead of the 2026 elections. This differs from the 2025 tariff, which was struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court for relying on the emergency IEEPA authority. Only 21% of Brazil’s exports to the U.S. are exposed to the new tariff, with 54% already exempt and additional portions subject to separate Section 232 duties on steel, aluminum and automobiles.

item.title: Flávio diz que não viu vídeo de Michelle: "Não tenho relação com ela"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated he has no relationship with Michelle Bolsonaro after she published a video criticizing him, saying he did not watch it to avoid being 'contaminated'. He emphasized that his mission comes directly from former President Jair Bolsonaro and said the door remains open for Michelle to join his presidential campaign, despite their current estrangement.

item.title: Expulso e reintegrado ao DC, Aldo Rebelo mantém pré-campanha à Presidência: 'situação está judicializada'
item.description: Aldo Rebelo, expelled and later reinstated in the Christian Democracy (DC) party, says his pre-presidential campaign continues as the party's candidate decision remains judicially determined. He criticized party president João Caldas for attempting to replace him with Joaquim Barbosa, noting Barbosa has not confirmed candidacy and that polls show weak performance for all DC pre-candidates. Rebelo stated he is touring the country in pre-campaign and insists the candidate must be chosen at the party convention between July 20 and August 5.

item.title: EUA confirmam novo tarifaço de 25% sobre produtos brasileiros
item.description: The U.S. imposed a new 25% tariff on Brazilian exports, excluding meat and coffee, following a Section 301 investigation that cited unfair trade practices, including policies favoring Pix. The measure, anticipated by the Lula government, comes amid ongoing trade tensions that previously included reciprocal 10% tariffs in April 2025. Brazil is considering a retaliatory response, while figures like Flávio Bolsonaro attended hearings as observers.

item.title: EUA confirmam novo tarifaço de 25% contra o Brasil
item.description: The United States imposed a new 25% tariff on Brazilian products, concluding a year-long trade investigation. The Lula government views the measure as unjustified and is seeking to expand exemptions, particularly for meat and coffee, while evaluating countermeasures such as the 2025 Economic Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Trump cumpre ameaça e impõe tarifa de 25% a produtos brasileiros
item.description: The United States imposed a 25% tariff on approximately 4,000 Brazilian products, with an estimated impact of $14.9 billion on Brazilian exports to the U.S. The measure, based on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, accuses Brazil of unfair practices in areas such as digital trade, ethanol, intellectual property, and illegal deforestation, including criticism of Pix and the Central Bank. The Lula government calls the decision technically unfounded and politically motivated, despite the U.S. maintaining a trade surplus with Brazil.

item.title: Temer diz que carta de Bolsonaro pode levar à perda da prisão domiciliar
item.description: Former President Michel Temer stated that a letter authored by Jair Bolsonaro and read by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during a live stream may have violated the conditions of Bolsonaro's house arrest, potentially leading to its revocation. Temer suggested the letter’s content could constitute a breach of judicial restrictions imposed in the ongoing investigations against the former president.
